game.title: The Evil Within
game.build_notes: Verified on Windows 10, 2026-09-03, with our winmm.dll proxy present. Driven entirely by external synthetic input against the game window; no in-process code was needed for navigation.

api_notes: Same primitives as the ENSLAVED profile: scancodes, KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY for arrows, foreground the window first, and capture with BitBlt rather than PrintWindow.
The game window is titled exactly 'The Evil Within' and BitBlt captures it cleanly.

bindings.notes: The splash says PRESS ANY KEY and appears before the title menu on every launch.
Menus print their controls on screen: '[ENTER] SELECT [ESC] BACK'.

states.name: photosensitivity_splash
states.detect: Black screen, red 'PHOTOSENSITIVITY WARNING', 'PRESS ANY KEY'. Frame delta is ~0 - it does not animate.

states.name: title_menu
states.detect: 'TITLE MENU' with CONTINUE / NEW GAME / LOAD GAME / OPTIONS / CREDITS / EXIT over a corridor scene.

states.name: pause_menu
states.detect: 'PAUSE' plus the chapter name top-left; ARCHIVE / TUTORIAL / LOAD GAME / RESTART CHAPTER / OPTIONS / TITLE MENU.

states.name: gameplay
states.detect: Third-person over-shoulder view, continuous non-zero frame delta.

steps: title menu appears with CONTINUE already highlighted
Down x5 (extended) to TITLE MENU - VERIFY the highlight, RESTART CHAPTER is in the path
confirm dialog appears with NO highlighted - press Up to select YES, verify, Enter
wait for the title menu to load
Down x5 to EXIT - VERIFY, NEW GAME sits two rows above
second confirm dialog, again defaulting to NO - Up, verify, Enter
routes.notes: Process exits ~2s after the final confirm. This is the graceful close.

console.notes: Steam launch options on this install carry '+com_allowconsole'. One tilde press produced no console, but the game had dropped to its attract screen at the time, so that is n=1 against an unfavourable state rather than a test. Not pursued: this project drives the game through its own winmm proxy, so a console is not needed.

proxy_env_vars.notes: The project's winmm.dll proxy is configured by environment variables read AT PROCESS START: TEWVR_TEST_YAW, TEWVR_DUMP, TEWVR_SHADERDUMP, TEWVR_SEQDUMP, TEWVR_CBPEEK, TEWVR_FINDCAM, TEWVR_FRAMECAPTURE, TEWVR_TARGETOFF, TEWVR_TARGETSIZE, TEWVR_SEQDUMP_ARMFILE. Because they are read at start, none can be armed mid-session - each needs a fresh launch. Launcher: staging/the-evil-within-vr/tools/launch-yaw-test.bat || CRITICAL, learned the hard way 2026-09-03: a launch FROM STEAM does not carry these variables, so the proxy silently runs with defaults and the log says so ('TEWVR_TEST_YAW unset/0 -> K = identity'). Confirmed from the process table: parent was steam.exe. There is NO runtime channel to arm them - the proxy's file triggers (capture.txt, seqarm.txt, skipcl.txt) were checked and none arms the yaw. So when asking for a relaunch that needs one of these, NAME THE LAUNCHER EXPLICITLY and say that starting from Steam will not work; 'please relaunch' is not enough.

hazards.hazard: BOTH confirmation dialogs default to NO
hazards.notes: 'Are you sure you want to quit? Any unsaved progress will be lost.' highlights NO, in the pause-menu route AND again on the title-menu EXIT. A blind Enter cancels and reads exactly like an ignored keypress. Press Up first and verify the highlight before committing.

hazards.hazard: Destructive items sit in the navigation path
hazards.notes: NEW GAME is directly below CONTINUE on the title menu, and RESTART CHAPTER is in the path from ARCHIVE down to TITLE MENU on the pause menu. Navigate, capture, verify the highlight, then commit.

hazards.hazard: TITLE MENU from the pause menu says 'quit' but returns to the title screen
hazards.notes: The confirm text reads 'Are you sure you want to quit?', but it unloads to the title menu rather than exiting the process. Exiting to desktop needs a second pass through EXIT on the title menu. Do not conclude the process failed to close.

hazards.hazard: The game returns to an ATTRACT screen if left idle at the title
hazards.notes: A scene plays with 'PRESS ANY KEY' overlaid. It looks like gameplay in a screenshot but accepts only a keypress, and a frame delta against it can be large enough to be mistaken for a real state change. Press any key to return to the title menu.
